proof: If $\mathcal H$ contains a $d$-cube, restrict an interpolating polynomial to that cube.  Every real-valued function on the cube must then be representable; in particular its parity function requires degree $d$.  Hence $\mathrm{intdeg}(\mathcal H)\ge\mathrm{ST}(\mathcal H)$.
witness_verification: For any Addressing class with n>=2, the n private coordinate functions are the delta functions of the n targets, so every function on the class has a degree-one interpolant; degree zero cannot interpolate all functions on a nontrivial class. Thus interpolation degree is exactly one (value 351). Two different concepts disagree at both of their private coordinates, so the one-inclusion graph has no edge and the largest strongly shattered set has size zero (value 28). This gives the strict endpoint inequality 1>0 on the stated nontrivial scope, independently of the bit encoding.
name: Interpolation degree / Largest Strongly Shattered Set
